basis: Radiation damages marrow; dermal atrophy in 80-99% supports skin involvement. Vomiting/diarrhea alone do not establish intestinal injury; severe neurologic injury is dose-dependent.
Premature skin/subcutaneous aging and skeletal abnormalities characterize most forms; vascular and neurologic injury vary substantially across subtypes.
Malignancy occupying lymphoid tissue, including primary lymphoid and metastatic tumors. The umbrella is not uniformly lymphoma, so an immune mechanism is not universal.
Inherited porphyrin metabolic disorder with defining cutaneous phototoxicity. Anemia, gallstones and liver enzyme abnormalities are each reported in 5-29%.
Umbrella of infections transmitted by ticks; no additional damaged organ is shared by most constituent diseases.
Intellectual disability and growth hormone deficiency define the syndrome, each present in 80-99%; skeletal maturation abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Poikiloderma and cataracts define RTS1; skeletal anomalies and dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Endocrine abnormalities are subgroup-specific or below 30% overall.
Congenital atrioventricular septal and valve defects. Pulmonary venous hypertension is vascular; hepatomegaly and respiratory symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.
Benign tumor arising in the pharynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis under the specified mapping.
Malignant tumor of the diencephalon; no additional organ involvement is established across the group.
Carcinoma arising from lung epithelium; distant organ involvement is stage-dependent and not intrinsic to the umbrella diagnosis.
Congenital remnant of the urachus, part of urinary tract development. Infection and obstruction are complications rather than universal defining mechanisms.
Benign digestive tract and associated gland tumors; gastrointestinal sites predominate. Hepatobiliary origin applies only to a subset.
UROS-related congenital erythropoietic porphyria causes metabolic dysfunction, destructive photosensitivity and hemolytic anemia. Tooth pigmentation and hepatomegaly alone do not prove injury.
Cranial dysinnervation and developmental impairment define disease. Profound deafness occurs in 1/1, cochlear hypoplasia in 1/2, and corneal opacity in 1/2; estimates use very small samples.
Congenital bowing of long bones defines the disorder. Unspecified skin abnormalities lack evidence of common direct damage.
Creatine transport defect causes neurodevelopmental dysfunction. Aganglionic megacolon/ileus occur in 30-79%; prolonged QT in 7/18 (~39%) supports cardiac electrical dysfunction.
Prolactin-secreting neoplasm arising in the anterior pituitary. Visual pathway damage is not common across all tumor sizes.
B2M deficiency causes excessive albumin/IgG catabolism and immunodeficiency. Bronchiectasis in 2/2 supports common structural airway damage, although the sample is small.
Inherited bile-acid metabolism/transport disorder. Elevated circulating bile acids alone do not establish common structural or functional liver injury across subtypes.
Isolated sperm flagellar defects causing male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease is established.
Lysosomal storage disorder with rapid neurodegeneration. Progressive retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients during the typical course.
Isolated developmental reduction in eye size caused by GDF3 variants; no consistent extraocular disease is established.
Inherited cutaneous hypopigmentation defines the condition; no other organ involvement is documented.
Erythrocytosis/gammopathy and immune-mediated vascular disease; shunting/pleural disease in 80-99% impairs respiration. Perinephric collections and other manifestations omitted at the four-axis cap.
